_comment: Which pages carry the five-market appendix, and which do not.
The appendix is the block built by APPENDIX in tools/build-modunera-depth.mjs:
a card per destination market naming the competent authority, the governing
plan, whether permanent living is possible, the delivery price and the import
VAT rate; then the MD 1-MD 8 table; then the five-point ordering checklist.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
It was applied to every page in the article library, which put roughly 640
words and forty sentences of country permitting onto 221 pages, 144 of them
indexed. Measured on the indexed set, the same permit paragraph appeared on
146 pages and the same checklist on 144. On a page about kitchen layout or
acoustic separation, Danish sommerhusomraade zoning answers a question the
reader did not ask, and it is the single largest source of repetition among
the 514 pages the site actually offers to search.
THE RULE
Keep it where siting, permitting, import or total cost is the subject of the
page. Drop it everywhere else. Default is DROP: a page type that is not named
here does not get the appendix, so adding a tree cannot silently inherit it.
The nine article categories are paired de/en explicitly rather than by index,
so reordering either corpus cannot quietly flip a decision.
topic_overrides exists because one category is not uniform: comparison and
alternatives is mostly style comparison, where the appendix is off-topic, but
'tiny house versus caravan' and 'tiny house versus modular house' both turn on
the building-or-vehicle distinction that the country cards are the answer to.
Those two topics keep it; the category does not.
Measured after this file was applied: see docs/seo-geo-ai-report.md and
node tools/score-indexed-originality.mjs.

categories.why: The appendix is this subject. Authority, governing plan and whether permanent living is allowed are the four things these pages are about.
Each country card carries the delivery price and the import VAT rate for that market, which is the material of this category.
Delivery per market and the budget checklist — foundation, connections, unloading, fees, insurance — are cost material, not padding, on a costs page.
Every card states whether permanent living, holiday use or letting is permitted. For a letting or glamping business that is the deciding fact, not background.
Insulation, glazing, fire, ventilation, the steel frame. Danish zoning does not bear on a build-up, and forty sentences of it displaced the subject.
Kitchen, bathroom, storage, acoustics, sleeping arrangements. Nothing on these pages is decided by a commune's land-use plan.
Heating, solar, power, water. Off-grid supply is a technical subject; the permitting question belongs on the pages that are about permitting.
Cleaning, damp, cladding care, servicing. These are read after the house exists, when the permit question is long settled.
Mostly style comparison — chalet, modern, Scandinavian. See topic_overrides for the two subjects in it that are genuinely permitting questions.

topic_overrides.why: Tiny house against caravan is decided by whether the thing is a vehicle or a building, which is exactly what the country cards state.
Same distinction: what separates the two in practice is the permitting route, not the construction.

trees.why: The thirteen German Europe guides: permits per country, customs, transport, plot, budget, letting, year-round climate. The appendix is their summary.
The same thirteen guides in English, plus the manufacturer comparison.
These hubs index the market guides and nothing else, so the appendix is the index of what they index.
The Europe FAQ. The five-market question is the page.
A bungalow or a module set on a plot is a building. Where it may stand and who decides that is the reader's next question, in every one of the five markets.

dropped_trees.why: A steel frame and a fitted kitchen are supplied into someone else's project. The buyer is not asking a commune whether they may own a wardrobe.
The capability index. Its job is to route to six pages, and each of those answers the permitting question where it applies.
Library hubs spanning all nine categories. They carry their own indexes and are long enough without it.
The general FAQ already answers the permit question in its own words; faq/europa is the page that keeps the appendix.
Catalogue and advantages pages. Neither is about where the house may stand.
